task.description: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 3b) hard gate on REQ-155's test coverage.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 REQ-155 acceptance criteria have real runnable test coverage, verified independently
The two reported gap fixes (T7/AC-6, T8/AC-7 moduledoc-content assertions) confirmed present and would actually catch a violation

ac_verification.AC-1: T1 (executor_test.exs:261) drives timeout_ms 100 vs 600 on the same infinite loop, asserts distinct returned wallclock_timeout values and elapsed-time ordering. Real, would fail if hardcoded.
ac_verification.AC-2: T2 (line 318) pcall-then-goto-loop script; asserts {:error,{:wallclock_timeout,300}} not budget_exceeded/ok. Verified deviation from spec's original T2 is documented in test/specs/REQ-155.md with a concrete, plausible technical rationale (permanently-tripped :max_instructions counter vs uninstrumented goto).
ac_verification.AC-3: T3 (line 335) before/after Task.Supervisor.children/1 snapshot equality after a timeout-terminated call. Confirmed by my own grep that Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor is referenced only by lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex, and this one test file -- no cross-file interference risk, matching the spec's claim.
ac_verification.AC-4: T4 (line 358) + T5 (line 374) each assert their own shape and refute the other's shape plus bare-string/atom arms.
ac_verification.AC-5: T6 (line 388, runtime) + T6-doc (line 414) -- runtime test proves in-flight child presence; doc test asserts moduledoc names both Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor and Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor. I independently read executor.ex's moduledoc lines 66-79 and confirmed a real, substantive justification for the separate supervisor is present, not just the two names.
ac_verification.AC-6: T7 (line 423). Independently confirmed against executor.ex's actual moduledoc: 'LUA-10' (line 30/37), 'layer 2' (line 32), 'enforced by the host' (line 37), 'cooperate' (line 38/45), and the literal gap-closing substring 'Neither LUA-08 nor LUA-10 is met' -- present verbatim at moduledoc line 33 ('Neither LUA-08 nor LUA-10 is met until both layers have landed together'). Gap fix confirmed real: the four original substrings alone are satisfiable without ever stating the 'neither is met without both' clause, and the added assertion now pins exactly that clause.
ac_verification.AC-7: T8 (line 439). Independently confirmed against executor.ex moduledoc: 'System.halt/0' (line 87, inside backticks, substring still matches), 'BEAM node' (line 86), and the exact gap-closing substring 'does **NOT** cover a hard kill of the BEAM node' -- present verbatim at moduledoc lines 86 ('This does **NOT** cover a hard kill of the BEAM node itself, or'). Gap fix confirmed real: a bare 'NOT' substring could match unrelated negation elsewhere in a long moduledoc; the new assertion ties the negation to its actual subject.
ac_verification.AC-8: Not a unit-test criterion -- correctly deferred to TEST-RUNNER per WF-02 Step 4, consistent with normal workflow division.

other_checks.todo_skip_markers: None found. grep -n 'TODO|@tag :skip|@tag skip' across test/specs/REQ-155.md and executor_test.exs returned no matches.
other_checks.hardcoded_secrets: None found. grep for password/secret/api_key/token/connection-string patterns returned no matches.
other_checks.fixture_isolation: No Application.put_env or other shared mutable global-state mutation in the REQ-155 describe block (grep confirmed). All tests use the /3-arity execute_with_manifest overload with explicit opts, independent of Application config.
other_checks.execution_order_independence: Confirmed: T3/T6's Task.Supervisor.children/1 snapshot comparisons rely only on Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor being used by no other test file (independently grep-verified) and on ExUnit's default sequential execution within one Case module -- no test depends on another test having run first.

result.toolchain_note: mix/elixir/erl are not present in this environment (which not found; no mix binary reachable) -- could not independently re-run `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` myself. Verification here is by direct static reading of both the test file and the actual executor.ex moduledoc source, including literal substring confirmation for the two reported gap fixes, per the core-directive to state toolchain unavailability explicitly rather than assume a result.
result.verdict: PASS. All 8 REQ-155 acceptance criteria have real, independently-verified test coverage. Both reported gap fixes (T7/AC-6, T8/AC-7) are present in executor_test.exs and I independently confirmed, by reading the actual moduledoc text in lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex, that every asserted substring (including the two literal gap-closing strings) genuinely occurs there -- these assertions would fail against a moduledoc that dropped either clause. No TODO/skip markers, no hardcoded secrets, no cross-test fixture pollution, no execution-order dependency.
